_comment: Durable pin for the FORMALIZED trust anchor: the Lean kernel re-checker. This file's bytes are folded into LeanVerifier.binary_hash, so changing the checker pin mints a new verifier identity and drops prior certification stamps.
mode: default (trusts imported oleans; replays the target module's OWN added declarations through the real kernel starting from the environment provided by its imports)
rationale: The FORMALIZED gate must KERNEL-RE-CHECK the compiled module, not merely audit which axioms a term cites. `Lean.collectAxioms` over an attacker-mutated Environment is the wrong instrument: a source can inject a constant with a FALSE type but a clean, axiom-free value via `(getEnv).addDeclCore (doCheck := false)`, `Environment.add`, or `set_option debug.skipKernelTC true; addDecl`, so collectAxioms reports `axioms: []` for a proof of False.

`lean4checker` (github.com/leanprover/lean4checker) is the standard external tool that re-checks an olean's environment through the real kernel, detecting exactly these environment-hacking injections. It is what mathlib CI uses.

As of Lean v4.28.0 the tool was MERGED INTO the Lean toolchain and is now distributed with every toolchain as `leanchecker` (the standalone leanprover/lean4checker repo is DEPRECATED and pending archival). See its README.

Because the checker is version-locked to the olean binary format, the version-matched instrument for our pinned v4.31.0 project is the `leanchecker` shipped IN the v4.31.0 toolchain. Building the deprecated external repo would be UNSOUND here: its newest ref is master @ v4.29.0-rc8 (no v4.30/v4.31 tag or branch exists upstream), and a v4.29 checker cannot load a v4.31 olean.
Thus the pin is the toolchain itself (already pinned by lean/EmpiricistLean/lean-toolchain), and the checker is `$(lake env which leanchecker)` resolved from that toolchain.

deprecated_external_repo.status: deprecated; merged into Lean toolchain as `leanchecker` since v4.28.0
deprecated_external_repo.not_used_reason: version mismatch with our v4.31.0 oleans; superseded by the built-in leanchecker
